title: Twin Earth NYC Event Bus Message
description: An event bus message is the fundamental unit of inter-system communication in the Twin Earth NYC simulation. All subsystems (IoT artifacts, NPC AI, heat engine, ledger, portal manager, authority response, rendering) communicate through a publish-subscribe event bus. Each message has a hierarchical topic (domain.type.action), a payload that varies by topic, a priority level, a time-to-live, and acknowledgment tracking. The event bus is the nervous system of the simulation — it connects sensors to actuators, events to responses, and observations to ledger entries.

message_id.description: Globally unique message identifier. Format: MSG_{hex-hash}. Example: MSG_b4e2c0a7.

topic.description: Hierarchical message topic in the format domain.type.action. Subscribers filter on topic patterns (wildcards supported). Examples: 'traffic.signal.state_change', 'security.camera.motion_detected', 'portal.lifecycle.state_change', 'heat.region.level_change', 'npc.behavior.goal_change', 'ledger.event.committed', 'authority.response.dispatched'.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the message was published to the bus.

source_entity_id.description: Entity ID of the entity that generated this message. For system-level messages, this is a synthetic entity ID representing the subsystem (e.g., 'SYS_HEAT_ENGINE', 'SYS_PORTAL_MANAGER').

source_subsystem.description: Name of the subsystem that published this message. Examples: 'artifact_layer', 'npc_ai', 'heat_engine', 'portal_manager', 'ledger', 'authority_response', 'world_state', 'player_input'.

payload.description: Message payload. Structure varies by topic. The payload carries all data needed for subscribers to act on the message. Common payload patterns include: state change payloads (old_state, new_state, reason), detection payloads (detected_entity_id, confidence, location), lifecycle payloads (phase, trigger, metadata). See topic-specific documentation for payload schemas.

payload_schema_ref.description: Optional URI reference to the JSON Schema that validates this message's payload. Enables runtime payload validation.

priority.description: Message delivery priority. 'low' = batch-processable, can be delayed. 'normal' = standard delivery, processed in order. 'high' = expedited delivery, jumps ahead of normal messages. 'critical' = immediate processing required, interrupts current work. Examples: weather changes are 'low', NPC goal changes are 'normal', security breaches are 'high', portal collapses are 'critical'.

ttl_ms.description: Time-to-live in milliseconds. After this duration, the message is discarded if not yet consumed. 0 = no expiration (persistent message). Short TTLs are used for ephemeral state (real-time sensor readings). Long TTLs for important events (ledger commits, authority responses).

acknowledged.description: Whether at least one subscriber has acknowledged processing this message. Used for delivery guarantees on critical messages. Unacknowledged critical messages may be re-delivered.

processing_time_ms.description: Time taken by this subscriber to process the message.

result.description: Processing result. 'success' = fully processed. 'partial' = partially handled. 'error' = processing failed. 'ignored' = subscriber decided message was not relevant.

acknowledgments.description: Detailed acknowledgment log from each subscriber that processed this message.

correlation_id.description: Optional correlation identifier linking related messages across a causal chain. All messages triggered by the same root event share a correlation_id for distributed tracing.

reply_to_topic.description: Optional topic for response messages. Used in request-reply patterns where the publisher expects a response.

headers.description: Optional key-value headers for routing, filtering, and metadata. Examples: {'region': 'midtown', 'universe_id': 'UNI_BASELINE', 'trace_id': 'abc123'}.

sequence_number.description: Monotonically increasing sequence number within the topic partition. Used for ordering guarantees and duplicate detection.

partition_key.description: Key used to determine which partition handles this message. Typically the region or entity ID, ensuring that messages about the same entity/region are processed in order.

retry_count.description: Number of times this message has been re-delivered after failed processing.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retry attempts before the message is sent to the dead letter queue.

dead_lettered.description: Whether this message has been moved to the dead letter queue after exceeding max retries.

created_at.description: System timestamp when this message record was created (may differ from the event timestamp if there is processing delay).
